2 mega-cap stocks with exciting potential and 1 we avoid

Megacap stocks dominate their sectors and their actions influence economies worldwide. The flip side though is that their sheer size means they have less room for explosive growth as scale works against them.

Sound complicated? With StockStory, it doesn't have to be. Our job is to find you high-quality companies that can win regardless of the conditions. Keeping that in mind, here are two industry titans with attractive long-term potential and one that could be stalling.

One mega-cap stock to sell:
Walmart (WMT)

Market cap: $962 billion

Known for its large-format Supercenters, Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) is a retail pioneer that serves a budget-conscious consumer who is looking for a wide range of products under one roof.

Why Are We Wary of WMT?

The company has faced growth challenges as its 5.3% annual revenue increases over the last three years fell short of other consumer retail companies

Widely-available products (and therefore stiff competition) result in an inferior gross margin of 24.9% that must be offset through higher volumes

Responsiveness to unforeseen market trends is restricted due to its substandard operating margin profitability

Walmart's stock price of $123.24 implies a valuation ratio of 39.5x forward P/E. If you're considering WMT for your portfolio, see our FREE research report to learn more.

Two mega-cap stocks to watch:
Microsoft (MSFT)

Market cap: $3.94 trillion

Originally named "Micro-soft" for microcomputer software when founded in 1975, Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) is a global technology company that develops software, cloud services, devices, and AI solutions for consumers, businesses, and organizations worldwide.

Why Should You Buy MSFT?

Microsoft is one of the great brands not just in tech but all of business. It produces mission-critical software and bundles it together, resulting in cream-of-the-crop gross margins.

The company's elite unit economics lead to robust profit margins that improve over time. This speaks to the scale advantages and operating efficiency across its diverse portfolio, which spans everything from Office and Azure to Minecraft.

Microsoft has a virtuous cycle of returns. Its dominant market position enables it to generate strong free cash flow, and it reinvests these funds into promising ventures that further strengthen its competitive moat.

Microsoft is trading at $529.25 per share, or 25.6x forward price-to-earnings. Is now the right time to buy? See for yourself in our full research report, it's free.

title: Walmart investigates Flipkart over whistleblower kickback allegations – report
detail:
Walmart investigates Flipkart over whistleblower kickback allegations – report
Walmart has launched its third investigation at Flipkart in less than three years · Retail Insight Network
Shubhendu Vimal
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 11:24 AM EDT 2 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart is conducting an internal investigation at Flipkart following whistleblower complaints alleging kickbacks of more than Rs1.50bn ($15.7m), Moneycontrol reported, citing unnamed sources.

The probe concerns staff in Flipkart's smartphones and luggage and travel accessories divisions.

According to the report, the alleged misconduct involved employees receiving benefits from brands in exchange for assisting certain sellers and vendors on the platform.

Some of the suspected activity is said to be linked to Flipkart's business-to-business operations.

Walmart is Flipkart's parent and owns more than 80% of the Indian e-commerce company.

A source told Moneycontrol: "The employees were found to be largely exploiting the business-to-business (B2B) route at Flipkart. Some Flipkart employees took a cut from vendors of certain mobile phone brands when devices were moving from one business to another."

One source cited by the publication said the investigation remained in progress and that the scale and precise nature of the alleged wrongdoing, including the amount received by some employees in kickbacks, would become clearer in the coming weeks. Walmart would then take action.

Walmart has launched its third investigation at Flipkart in less than three years.

Taking place over two years ago, the first examined alleged financial misappropriation in the luggage and travel accessories unit and led to the dismissal of at least three employees.

A second inquiry, carried out around six months ago in the smartphones division, resulted in one employee leaving after being found guilty of the allegations.

The latest investigation comes as Flipkart faces other issues, including senior exits, concerns among current and former employees over employee stock ownership plan liquidity, and uncertainty around the timing of a possible IPO.

Moneycontrol previously reported that at least 14 vice-presidents and senior vice-presidents had departed in the past year while at least 1,000 former employees had written to Walmart's board seeking parity with current staff in the event of a stock buyback.

"Walmart investigates Flipkart over whistleblower kickback allegations – report" was originally created and published by Retail Insight Network, a GlobalData owned brand.

title: DoorDash's Acquisition of Instacart Will Take Time but is the Right Move, Wedbush Says
detail:
PREMIUM
DoorDash's Acquisition of Instacart Will Take Time but is the Right Move, Wedbush Says
MT Newswires
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 11:17 AM EDT 1 min read
DASH
CART
AMZN
WMT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

DoorDash's (DASH) acquisition of Maplebear (CART), doing business as Instacart, will take time but presents a consolidation play that bolsters its grocery strategy, as Instacart's differentiated technology should be a boost to the company, Wedbush said in a Friday research note.

The deal could close by early 2028, and Instacart's enterprise and advertising tools are expected to be accretive to DoorDash's fastest-growing part of its business, likely making it more competitive against Amazon (AMZN) and Walmart (WMT), analysts wrote.

Instacart adds demand to DoorDash's network, driving better density, positioning the combined entity to more effectively capture market share, according to Wedbush.

DoorDash reported a Q3 net income Thursday of $1.06 per diluted share, up from $0.55 a year earlier. Analysts polled by FactSet expected $0.81. Revenue for the three months ended Sept. 30 rose to $4.62 billion from $3.45 billion a year earlier. Analysts expected $4.56 billion.

The global technology replatforming is on track for completion in H1 2027, and modules already live are enhancing merchant onboarding, support response times, and search conversion, according to the note.

The brokerage said it upgraded the stock to outperform from neutral and raised its price target to $230 per share from $220.
